cheng: Quick heads-up — after today's kernel-selection patch merged to canary, overall cache warmup hit-rate dropped ~18% on psi-1 workloads. Observed a lot more misses in the first 30 tokens of requests.

maria: Hmm. Any profiling traces? which part of the patch could affect cache keying or chunking? :thinking:

cheng: Short profile dump below. The new kernel changed sequence chunk boundaries (more aggressive chunk folding) and we still truncate hash input to first 64 bytes when deriving the cache key. That truncation combined with shifted chunk boundaries seems to increase same-prefix collisions.

sam: Can you paste sample logs so I can eyeball collisions?

cheng: ```
[2026-08-05T10:12:03Z] model=psi-1 seq_len=64 tenant=acme key=sha256:7f2a9d... hit=false
[2026-08-05T10:12:03Z] model=psi-1 seq_len=64 tenant=acme key=sha256:9b6d4f... hit=false
[2026-08-05T10:12:03Z] model=psi-1 seq_len=64 tenant=beta  key=sha256:7f2a9d... hit=true
```
Noticed same prefix hash across tenants when chunk boundaries shift. I ran collision_check.sh over the canary logs: baseline collision rate ~0.0038 (24h) but during warmup windows spike to ~0.02.

lia: sec-bot reported cross-tenant collisions yesterday as well. @sec-bot any details?

sec-bot: automated-alert: cross-tenant-cache-collision-rate spike detected: 0.019 (1h window) on psi-1 canary. Top collided prefix=sha256:7f2a9d..., correlated with kernel-change rev-cc1f. Metadata: sample_count=132, impacted_tenants=[acme,beta].

maria: Sounds like root cause is (a) hash-input truncation and (b) chunking behavior change. Short term mitigations: add tenant salt to key derivation (prepend tenant-id), increase hash input window from 64 -> 256 bytes, and tag entries with tenant namespace.

sam: Short-term I can rollback the kernel patch to stop the immediate churn. Long-term we should avoid relying on truncated raw prefixes for isolation. Adding tenant namespace is cheap.

cheng: Also thinking about warmup strategy: our warmup metrics assume stable prefix alignment. We should measure 'time_to_90pct_hit_rate' per-tenant and treat shifts as a signal to temporarily disable global aggressive batching.

lia: On the security side, adding tenant salt helps isolation but we also need encryption for entries belonging to regulated tenants. For audit purposes, log collision events to an internal S3 bucket with redacted keys (first/last 8 hex) and tenant IDs.

maria: I'll open an RFC with: salt format (tenant:v1), KMS per-tenant cost implications, perf microbenchmarks for salted keys, and the rollout plan (canary -> staged). Include the 'collision_check' as a gating metric.

sam: Rolling back now and will keep canary pinned to pre-cc1f until we validate tenant-salt flow. I’ll annotate the rollback in deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: rolled back rev-cc1f on psi-1 at 2026-08-05T10:40:12Z :white_check_mark:

cheng: Thanks — adding collision-check to nightly perf job and increasing telemetry granularity for per-prefix collision counts. If anyone has a quick script to estimate perf impact of adding salt vs hash-window increase, drop it here and I'll run it on the perf harness.

maria: I'll add a microbenchmark to the perf repo today (latency and mem-alloc for salted keys + HMAC vs plain SHA).

sam: Noted. Will monitor canary and flag regressions.

lia: For the RFC: include recommended retention for collision logs and who can access them (security + privacy only).

cheng: Great. Closing this thread after RFC is up. Thanks all.
